translation: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra called the Diamond Cutter Perfection of Wisdom
Herein is contained the Noble Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter.
In the language of India: Ārya Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Nāma Mahāyāna Sūtra.
In the Tibetan language: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra called the Diamond Cutter Perfection of Wisdom.
Homage to all Buddhas and bodhisattvas.
Setting
Thus did I hear at one time.
The Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī at Jetavana, the park of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks, and very many bodhisattva great beings.
Then, in the morning time, the Blessed One put on his lower robe and Dharma robe, took up his alms bowl, and went to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
Then the Blessed One, having gone to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms, partook of his meal and completed the action of eating,

Having given up later alms, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robe, washed his feet, sat cross-legged on the arranged seat, straightened his body, and remained, having established mindfulness to the fore.
Then many monks went to where the Blessed One was, and having approached him,
Blessed One, how should one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
How should one practice?
How should one hold the mind?
When he had spoken thus,
The Blessed One's Reply
The Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
Subhūti, excellent, excellent!
Subhūti, it is so, it is so.
The Tathāgata has benefited the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme benefit.
The Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme entrustment.
Therefore, Subhūti, listen well and hold it thoroughly in mind, and
I shall explain to you how one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should abide, how one should practice, and how one should hold the mind.
Having replied, "Blessed One, it is so,"
the venerable Subhūti listened to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:
Generating the Mind of Awakening

Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: 'However many sentient beings are subsumed by the subsumption of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, or born from a womb, or born from warmth and moisture, or miraculously born, or having form, or without form, or having perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings, all those I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.'
Even though immeasurable sentient beings are thus led to complete nirvāṇa, one should generate the mind thinking that no sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa.
Why is that? Because they would not be called a bodhisattva.

Why is that? Because, Subhūti, if one engages in the perception of a sentient being, engages in the perception of a life-force, or engages in the perception of a person, they are not to be called a bodhisattva.
Moreover, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in an entity.
They should practice generosity without abiding in anything.
They should practice generosity without abiding in form.
Likewise, they should practice generosity without abiding in sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, or phenomena.
Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity in such a way that they do not abide even in the perception of a sign.
Why is that?
The Method of Training in the Conduct of the Six Perfections
Subhūti, it is because the mass of merit of a bodhisattva who practices generosity without abiding is not easy to measure, Subhūti.
Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think it is easy to measure space in the eastern direction?
Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not.
The Blessed One said: Subhūti, likewise, is it easy to measure space in the south, the west, the north, the zenith, the direction below, the intermediate directions, and the ten directions?
Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.
The Blessed One said: Subhūti, likewise, it is because the mass of merit of a bodhisattva who practices generosity without abiding in anything is not easy to measure, Subhūti.
Teaching That the Form Body Is Accomplished Through Generosity and So Forth
Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think that the Tathāgata should be seen by the perfection of marks?
Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.
The Tathāgata should not be seen by the perfection of marks.
They bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and sat down to one side.
Also at that time, the venerable Subhūti had assembled in that very assembly and was seated there.
The Question Asked by the Venerable Subhūti
Then the venerable Subhūti rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right kneecap on the ground, and bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One.
He addressed the Blessed One with these words:

"Blessed One, it is wonderful how the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has benefited the bodhisattva great beings with all the supreme benefits, and how the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings with all the supreme entrustments. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!"
Why is that? Because whatever the Tathāgata has taught as the perfection of marks is itself no perfection of marks.
When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
Subhūti, to whatever extent there is the perfection of marks, to that extent there is falsehood.
To whatever extent there is no perfection of marks, to that extent there is no falsehood.
Thus, the Tathāgata should be viewed as being without marks and signs.
When he had spoken thus, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
Therefore, with this in mind, the Tathāgata has spoken: 'Those who know this Dharma discourse to be like a raft should abandon even phenomena, let alone non-phenomena.'
Furthermore, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti:
Subhūti, what do you think?
Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has fully awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?
Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught?
When he had spoken thus, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
Therefore, with this in mind, the Tathāgata has said: 'Those who know this Dharma discourse to be like a raft should abandon even phenomena, let alone non-phenomena.'
Subhūti, those who will obtain even a single mind of faith regarding such explanations of the sūtra as this, the Tathāgata knows them.
Subhūti, those are seen by the Tathāgata.
Subhūti, all those sentient beings will generate and completely gather an immeasurable mass of merit.
Why is that? Subhūti, it is because those bodhisattva great beings will not engage in the perception of a self,
they do not have the perception of a sentient being, they do not have the perception of a life-force, and they will not engage in the perception of a person.
Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings will also not engage in the perception of a phenomenon, nor will they engage in the perception of a non-phenomenon,
Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken, there is no phenomenon whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has fully awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
There is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught.
Why is that? Any phenomenon to which the Tathāgata has fully awakened or that he has taught cannot be grasped and cannot be expressed.
That is because it is neither a phenomenon nor the absence of a phenomenon.
Why is that? Because noble persons are distinguished by the unconditioned.
The Blessed One said, Subhūti, what do you think?
Likewise, generosity should be practiced without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, or even phenomena.
Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity in such a way that they are without abiding even in the perception of a sign.
They will also not engage in non-perception.
Why is that? Subhūti, if those bodhisattva great beings were to engage in the perception of a phenomenon, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
Even if they were to engage in the perception of a selfless phenomenon, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
Why is that? Subhūti, a bodhisattva should not erroneously grasp at a phenomenon, nor should they grasp at a non-phenomenon.

Blessed One, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being thoroughly destroyed, will there appear any sentient beings who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?

The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, do not speak like this, saying: 'In the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being thoroughly destroyed, will there appear any sentient beings who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?'"

Subhūti, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being thoroughly destroyed, there will appear bodhisattva great beings who possess ethical discipline, possess good qualities, and possess wisdom.
Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings have not served a single Buddha.
They have not planted roots of virtue under a single Buddha, but
Subhūti, there will appear those bodhisattva great beings who have served many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and planted roots of virtue under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.

If some son of noble family or daughter of noble family were to fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, do you think that son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis?
Subhūti replied, Blessed One, it would be much.
Sugata, it would be much.
That son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis.
Why is that? Because that very mass of merit is not a mass.
Therefore, the Tathāgata spoke of "a mass of merit, a mass of merit."
Subhūti, what do you think?
Does a stream-enterer think: I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer?
Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not so.
Why is that? Blessed One, it is because he has not entered into anything.
Therefore, he is called a stream-enterer.
He has not entered into form, nor into sound, nor into smell, nor into taste, nor into tangible objects, nor has he entered into phenomena.
Why is that? Because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of a once-returner.
Therefore, he is called a once-returner.
Blessed One, if a once-returner were to think, 'I have attained the fruit of a once-returner,' that itself would be his grasping at a self.
It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
Does a non-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a non-returner'?"

The Blessed One said: Subhūti, compared to a son of noble family or daughter of noble family filling this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and giving it as a gift, if someone takes up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse, explains it to others, and perfectly demonstrates it, they will generate a much greater mass of merit from that basis, countless and immeasurable.
Why is that? Subhūti, the unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening of the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas, arises from this,
because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.
Why is that? Subhūti, as for what are called "qualities of a Buddha, qualities of a Buddha," it is because the Tathāgata spoke of those qualities of a Buddha as non-existent;
therefore they are called "qualities of a Buddha."
Eight Entrants and Abiders
Therefore, he is called a "stream-enterer."
Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer were to think that he had attained the fruit of a stream-enterer, that itself would be his grasping at a self.
It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?
Does a once-returner think that he has attained the fruit of a once-returner?
Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.
He has not entered into forms, nor into sounds, nor into smells, nor into tastes, nor into tangible objects, nor has he entered into phenomena.
They will also not engage in perception or non-perception.
Subhūti replied, Blessed One, that is not so.
Why is that? Because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of a non-returner.
Therefore, he is called a non-returner.
The Blessed One said, Subhūti, what do you think?
Does an arhat think, I have attained arhatship?
Subhūti replied, Blessed One, that is not so.
The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?
If there were exactly as many Gaṅgā rivers as there are grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river, do you think that the grains of sand in them would be many?
Subhūti replied: Blessed One, if those Gaṅgā rivers themselves would be many, what need is there to speak of their grains of sand?
The Blessed One said: Subhūti, you should be convinced.
You should understand.
If some man or woman were to completely fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in those Gaṅgā rivers with the seven precious substances,
Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'arrays of Buddha-fields, arrays of Buddha-fields,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught them as being without those arrays.
Therefore, they are called 'arrays of Buddha-fields.'
Subhūti, therefore, a bodhisattva great being should generate the mind without abiding in this way:
They should generate the mind without abiding in anything whatsoever.
They should generate the mind without abiding in form.
They should generate the mind without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, and phenomena.
Because I do not abide in anything whatsoever, he does not declare me to be 'abiding without affliction'.
The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata obtained from the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara?"
Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, that is not so.
There is absolutely no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata obtained from the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara."
The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I will accomplish the arrays of Buddha-fields,' he would be speaking untruthfully.
Why is that? It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that is called an arhat.
Blessed One, if an arhat were to think, 'I have obtained arhatship,' that itself would be his grasping at a self,
it would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those abiding without affliction,
Blessed One, although I am an arhat free from desire, Blessed One, I do not think, 'I am an arhat.'
Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained arhatship,' the Tathāgata, concerning me, 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction,'
and were to give them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, Subhūti, what do you think? Would that man or woman generate much merit on that basis?
Subhūti replied, Blessed One, it would be much.
Sugata, it would be much.
That man or woman would generate much merit on that basis.
The Blessed One said, Subhūti, if someone were to completely fill that many world systems with the seven precious substances,

compared to giving them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, if someone were to take up even merely a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse, perfectly and thoroughly explain it to others, and perfectly and thoroughly teach it, that very person would generate much more merit on that basis, countless and immeasurable.

Subhūti, it is like this: for example, if a person were to have a body like this, that is, if it were to become as large as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, Subhūti, what do you think? Would you think that body is large?
Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that body would be large.
Sugata, that body would be large.
Why is that? Because the Tathāgata has taught that it is no entity.
Therefore, it is called a large body.
Because it is no entity, therefore it is called a body.
Therefore, they are called "arrays of Buddha-fields".
One should generate the mind without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, and phenomena.

Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and demigods, it goes without saying that whoever takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will become endowed with supreme wonder;
in that place resides the Teacher, or someone like a guru.
When this had been said, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
“Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma discourse?
How should I hold it?”
When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
Because I do not abide in anything whatsoever, he does not declare "abiding without affliction."
Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata."
The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
Do you think that the particles of earth that exist in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system are many?"
Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, those particles of earth are many.
Sugata, they are many.
Why is that? Blessed One, it is because whatever is a particle of earth has been taught by the Tathāgata as not a particle."
Subhūti, the name of this Dharma discourse is the perfection of wisdom;
you should hold it thus.
Why is that? Subhūti, because the very perfection of wisdom spoken by the Tathāgata is itself not a perfection.
Therefore, it is called the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti, what do you think?
Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever spoken by the Tathāgata?
Subhūti replied: "Blessed One, that is not so."
"Why is that? Because whatever thirty-two marks of a great man were spoken of by the Tathāgata, they were spoken of by the Tathāgata as no marks.
Therefore they are called the thirty-two marks of a great man."

The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand of the Gaṅgā river, and if someone were to take up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse and teach it properly to others, that person would generate on that basis far greater, incalculable, immeasurable merit."
Then venerable Subhūti shed tears by the force of the Dharma.
Having wiped away his tears, he said this to the Blessed One:
Therefore, it is called a "particle of earth."
Because whatever those world systems are, the Tathāgata has taught them as non-systems.
Therefore, it is called a "world system."
Marks and Minor Marks
The Blessed One said, Subhūti, what do you think?
Should the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?

Blessed One, in the future time, in the last five hundred years, those sentient beings who take up, write, hold, keep, read, and fully master this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.
Furthermore, Blessed One, they will not engage in the perception of a self,
and will not engage in the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, or the perception of a person.

Why is that? Because, Blessed One, whatever is the perception of a self, the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, and the perception of a person, that itself is devoid of all perceptions.
Why is that? Because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are devoid of all perceptions.
When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:

Why is that? Subhūti, at the time when the king of Kaliṅga severed my limbs and minor limbs, neither the perception of a self, nor the perception of a sentient being, nor the perception of a life-force, nor the perception of a person arose in me, and
because I had no perception whatsoever, and it was not the case that I was without perception.
Why is that? Subhūti, if at that time the perception of a self had arisen in me, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen, and
because if the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, or the perception of a person had arisen, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen.
Subhūti, I remember that in the past, when I was the sage called Kṣāntivādin for five hundred lifetimes, even at that time the perception of a self did not arise in me.
Neither the perception of a sentient being, nor the perception of a life-force, nor the perception of a person arose.
Blessed One, it is a marvel how extensively this Dharma discourse has been spoken by the Tathāgata. Sugata, it is a marvel.
Blessed One, ever since pristine wisdom arose in me, I have never before heard this Dharma discourse.
Why is that? Blessed One, those sentient beings who will generate a true perception regarding this sūtra being explained will be endowed with supreme marvel.
Why is that? Blessed One, it is because whatever is a true perception is itself a non-perception.
Therefore, the Tathāgata has spoken of 'true perception'.
Blessed One, that I contemplate and have faith in this Dharma discourse being explained is not a marvel to me.
Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva great being, having completely abandoned all perceptions,
should generate the mind for unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
They should generate the mind without abiding in form.
They should generate the mind without abiding in sound, smell, taste, or tangible objects.
They should generate the mind without abiding in phenomena.
They should generate the mind without abiding in non-phenomena.
Therefore, the Tathāgata speaks of 'true perception'.
Subhūti, so it is. So it is.
Those sentient beings who, when this sūtra is being explained, are not terrified, not frightened, and do not become completely frightened, will be endowed with supreme wonder.
Why is that? Subhūti, this supreme perfection was taught by the Tathāgata,
because whatever supreme perfections were taught by the Tathāgata, those were also taught by immeasurable, countless Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
Therefore, it is called the supreme perfection.
Moreover, Subhūti, whatever is the perfection of patience of the Tathāgata, that itself is no perfection.
One should generate the mind without abiding in anything at all.
Why is that? Because whatever is an abiding is itself without abiding.
Therefore, the Tathāgata has spoken thus: "A bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in anything at all."
Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should completely relinquish generosity in this way for the benefit of all sentient beings.
Whatever is the perception as a sentient being is itself a non-perception.
Those very sentient beings that the Tathāgata has spoken of as "all sentient beings" are themselves non-existent.
One should generate the mind without abiding in phenomena.
One should generate the mind without abiding in non-phenomena.
Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata speaks authentically, speaks truthfully, and speaks of suchness,
because the Tathāgata does not speak falsely.
Furthermore, Subhūti, in whatever phenomenon the Tathāgata has fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.

Subhūti, it is like this: for example, just as a person with sight who has entered into darkness sees nothing at all, in the same way should one view a bodhisattva who completely gives generosity having fallen into entities.

Furthermore, Subhūti, it is like this: for example, when dawn breaks and the sun rises, a person with sight sees various forms; in the same way should one view a bodhisattva who completely gives generosity without having fallen into entities.

Furthermore, Subhūti, whatever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up this Dharma discourse, hold it, keep it, read it, completely master it, and extensively and authentically teach it to others, those are known by the Tathāgata, and are seen by the Tathāgata,
they will be severely tormented.

Why is that? Subhūti, because those sentient beings are tormented in this very life for whatever non-virtuous actions they committed in previous lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms, those non-virtuous actions they committed in previous lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms will be purified,
and they will also attain the awakening of a Buddha.

Subhūti, I remember that in the past, measureless and even more than measureless eons ago, before and even further before the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara, eighty-four hundred thousand million myriad Buddhas appeared, whom I pleased,
and having not displeased them, did not disappoint them.

Subhūti, regarding whatever pleasing and not disappointing of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, I did, and whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, writes, upholds, keeps, reads, and completely comprehends this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.
all those sentient beings will generate an immeasurable mass of merit.

Moreover, Subhūti, if a man or a woman were to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during the morning, and were also to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during midday and during the afternoon, compared to completely giving away bodies in this manner for many hundreds of thousands of millions of eons,

if someone, having heard this Dharma discourse, does not abandon it, they would on that basis generate much more merit, countless and immeasurable. What need is there to mention someone who writes it down, takes it up, holds it, keeps it, reads it, completely masters it, and extensively and correctly teaches it to others?
Furthermore, Subhūti, this Dharma discourse is inconceivable and incomparable.
Its ripening should also be known to be inconceivable.

The Tathāgata has spoken this Dharma discourse for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the foremost vehicle.
The Tathāgata knows and the Tathāgata sees those who take up, hold, keep, read, master, and extensively and authentically teach this Dharma discourse to others;
all those sentient beings will be endowed with an immeasurable mass of merit,
they will be endowed with an inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, and limitless mass of merit,
All those sentient beings will carry my awakening upon their shoulders.
Why is that? Subhūti, this Dharma discourse cannot be heard by those who are inclined toward the inferior,
nor by those who hold the view of a self, nor by those who hold the view of a sentient being, nor by those who hold the view of a life-force,
and those who hold a view of a person are unable to listen to, take up, retain, read, or master it,
because that is impossible.
Moreover, Subhūti, any place where this sūtra is taught will become worthy of being venerated by the world with its gods, humans, and demigods.
That place will become worthy of being bowed to and worthy of being circumambulated,
that place will become like a stūpa.
Moreover, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up, retain, keep, read, and master these words of such a sūtra will be tormented,
and even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, it is because they are not to be called a bodhisattva.
Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever called 'having correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle'.
Subhūti, what do you think?
Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?
When he had spoken those words, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:
Blessed One, there is no phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
How should they practice?
How should the mind be fully held?
When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:

Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: 'I shall lead all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa in the expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.'
Even though immeasurable sentient beings have been led to complete nirvāṇa in this way, they should generate the mind thinking, 'No sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa.'
Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, they are not to be called a bodhisattva;
